$comment: Reader-facing version history, summarized by hand from 06_WHITEPAPER/v5, v6 and v7 changelogs. Add a row at the top for each new version. No file names, tooling or review process: only what changed for a reader.

versions.summary: Prior art re-checked. Section 5.2's measuring loop is labeled as this paper's arrangement of the 2026 SRE chapter's advice, and a few readings of the chapter are softened. Hixson and Guliani's “costs” are read as an early form of the coefficient, and Figure 6 is updated to match. Several points are made more precise where practitioners would push back: coefficients as a straight-line reading near today's load, redundancy set per cell with uneven failover, the next purchase pulled earlier by a marginal job, and buffers that multiply only if latency must hold during a failure.

Section 10 now opens with the handshake: capital, supply and demand, with the planner brokering it, and what the planner trades in. Figure 41 is redrawn as that triangle, with the three seams on its edges. Section 5.2 lays out the 2026 SRE chapter's measuring loop step by step, credited in full, and adds the price reading; Figure 10 is redrawn as two rings. Short notes on people practice are added across Sections 6, 9, 10, 12 and 14, with re-baselining as a routine step.

The 2026 SRE capacity planning chapter, read in full, is credited wherever it got there first. Nineteen new public sources, including the discipline's lineage in Section 3. Eight labeled explorations, offered as ways to think rather than findings. Two new figures: a pooled launch reserve (Figure 28) and the Meet case on two clocks (Figure 47). References renumbered by first appearance.

Most long sentences split into shorter ones. Each test in Section 9.4 moved onto the mechanism it checks, under “You'll know it's working when…”. Mechanism 3 renamed the coefficient register and versioned rate card. A version line, a note on what is meant to last, and a “What changed” table added to the front matter.

A new figure for the channel to challenge coefficients (Section 10.4). Earlier hedges on the method's status. With this version the figures and captions, read alone, carry every main point of the paper.

Figures carry the argument: flowcharts, swimlanes, a decision tree, a matrix, cycles and charts of public values. Each appendix rebuilt to stand on its own. The reference list renumbered by first appearance.
The visual program: one visual language for every figure, with errors in older figures corrected.

The layered format: abstract, executive summary, one page and deep dive. Two claims and a method stated plainly. New Section 8, the commit-point method. The supply side rewritten around public values. New Appendix A (a worksheet with a walk-through) and Appendix B (the public record on supply).

Rewritten in a practitioner's voice. Each section opens with something a planner has seen, then the mechanism, then the principle, with an “In short” line at the top. One picture per idea. Credit to Hixson and Guliani's 2015 article checked against the source and widened.
Step-change demand and supply merged in as an extension of the second claim: approval is not allocation in time, as well as in shape and place.
